cover.headline: A recovering forger priced for a full recovery and a re-rating: we see little left to pay for
cover.lead: Ramkrishna Forgings is India's second-largest forging company (forged and machined truck parts, gears, ring-rolled parts, castings and trailer axles; ~32% of standalone revenue exported). Its EPS fell from ₹16.1 in FY24 to ₹3.9 in FY26. That collapse was not one event: FY25's reported ₹22.9 hid a ₹170 cr inventory write-down (book stock overstated by errors and unrecorded rejections, found at the year-end count and confirmed by an independent fact-finding review) behind a ₹193 cr deferred-tax credit and an ₹83 cr gain on a sold subsidiary; FY26 then had no one-offs to hide a 20% fall in exports and a jump in depreciation and interest after ₹2,900 cr of capex and acquisitions. Q1FY27 (revenue +20%, 18% margin) is a real recovery, and we forecast EPS of ₹12.7 / ₹21.2 / ₹27.6 for FY27-29E. The street values the stock on **P/E on FY28E** (Dalal & Broacha 27x). The stock's own forward P/E median since 2021 on EPS before one-offs, with the two trough years (FY25-26) left out, is 14.6x; cut by the 8.8% auto-component de-rating that gives **13.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹24.4 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹532, DCF ₹384. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Q1FY27 revenue ₹1,217 cr (+19.8%), EBITDA margin 18.0% (14.6% a year earlier), PAT ₹47 cr (₹12 cr). Exports +11%, domestic +20%, subsidiaries +49%. Management guides ~₹8,000 cr of revenue by FY29 (22-25% a year), export growth of 20%+ and lower debt. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|n1}}% / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|n1}}% / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|n1}}% and margins of {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} → {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}, below the old 21-22%.

arguments.h: But trust has to be rebuilt
arguments.p: Book inventory was overstated by ₹220.5 cr at Mar-2025 (₹50.2 cr at Mar-2024, now restated) through erroneous SAP entries and rejections that were never recorded. No fraud was alleged, the promoters paid ₹205 cr for warrants at ~3.6x the market price to plug the hole, and controls were tightened; but ratings went to Negative/were cut, and the ₹8,000 cr target has already slipped a year.

arguments.h: Leverage and capital intensity cap the returns
arguments.p: Net debt ~₹1,900 cr (Jun-2026) is ~3x FY26 EBITDA; ROCE was 6% in FY26. Even on our recovery numbers ROE reaches only {{F.roe.2|pct}} in FY29E, below a ~12.5% cost of capital, because depreciation and interest absorb a third of EBITDA and working capital grows with revenue.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price is ~2x the stock's own history
arguments.p: At ₹702 the stock trades at 28.8x our Sep-28E EPS and ~122x trailing. On normal earnings it traded at 7-17x forward in 2021-23; the 15-35x readings of 2023-24 rest on FY25 EPS inflated by one-offs. Even the house median on reported EPS gives 20x (₹490) and adding back the FY25 inventory charge 24.5x (₹600): SELL either way. The street (Dalal & Broacha ₹663, consensus average ₹634) pays for a re-rating we cannot derive.

Rail-wheel JV: sample approval and bulk supply to Indian Railways from Sep/Oct-2026 (40,000-wheel FY27 offtake).
Net debt from ~₹1,900 cr (Jun-2026) towards the ~₹1,500 cr Mar-2027 target; rating outlook (CRISIL Negative).

sections.title: What Ramkrishna Forgings does: forged truck parts, two-thirds sold in India

blocks.p: Ramkrishna Forgings (RKFL), founded in 1981 in Kolkata and run by the Jalan family, is India's second-largest forging company. It heats steel bars and shapes them in dies (hammers, presses, ring-rolling mills, cold and warm forging), then machines many of the parts. Since FY25 it also casts iron parts. Customers are mainly commercial-vehicle (truck and bus) makers in India, North America and Europe, plus railways, mining and farm equipment, oil & gas and, recently, passenger cars and EVs. Installed capacity is 3,95,800 tonnes a year; FY26 production was 2,20,279 tonnes (~56%).

blocks.callout: **Pattern:** strong execution in the up-cycle, then problems when growth, acquisitions and new plants all came at once. The FY25 inventory overstatement built up in the year the company was integrating two acquisitions and commissioning capacity. It is the main reason we put more weight on the earnings record than on management's targets.

sections.title: Industry: Indian trucks at a record, US trucks at a bottom, energy and freight costs up

bullets: **India:** FY26 commercial-vehicle retail sales crossed 10 lakh for the first time (10,60,906, +11.74%); M&HCV production rose ~16% to 4,58,506. ICRA expects only 4-6% (ICRA, as quoted in the FY26 annual report) growth in FY27 off that high base.
**North America:** Class 8 retail sales were ~2.08-2.10 lakh units, down ~13-14% in 2025: A 'bottoming' year: weak freight demand, high costs, tariff uncertainty; strong close to the year.

**Tariffs:** US tariffs on Indian goods and Section 232 duties on truck parts hit FY26 exports (standalone exports -20%, North America -35%); management said in May-2026 that 'the tariff is behind us' and contracts pass currency and steel through with a quarter's lag.
**Costs:** Energy (gas, power) and shipping are the main unrecovered costs: shipping +15-20% and transit +15-20 days after the West Asia conflict (Q4FY26 call, May-2026).

**Competition:** Bharat Forge is far larger; Happy Forgings, GNA Axles and CIE Automotive compete in parts of the range. Global OEMs buy from several qualified suppliers; India's cost advantage is real but so is the customers' bargaining power.

blocks.callout: **So what:** RKFL's domestic business rides a strong Indian truck cycle that is now mature; its export business depends on a US truck recovery and on tariff policy, both outside its control.

blocks.p: Standalone domestic revenue grew from ₹1,995 cr (FY24) to ₹2,542 cr (FY26) as Indian truck production hit records and RKFL won railway, mining and PV business. sections.title: The profit collapse: an inventory write-down hidden by one-offs, then a tariff year with none

blocks.p: Peer screens (including our own Bharat Forge initiation) leave RKFL out because "its profit collapsed". The record: reported EPS went ₹16.1 (FY24) → ₹22.9 (FY25) → ₹3.9 (FY26), which looks like a sudden collapse in FY26. In fact FY25 was already weak. During the FY25 year-end physical count the company found that book inventory of work-in-progress, raw material and scrap exceeded physical stock. A joint fact-finding study by independent external agencies (forensic imaging of devices, interviews of SAP custodians) reported on 14-Jun-2025 that 'erroneous accounting entries and non-recording of rejections at the manufacturing plants' had overstated inventory by Rs220.52 cr at 31-Mar-2025 and Rs50.22 cr at 31-Mar-2024. Fully given effect in the FY25 standalone and consolidated accounts, including restatement of the FY24 comparatives (so FY24 as now shown is restated). Net-worth hit ~Rs202 cr (6.7%) per press reports. No fraud or misappropriation was alleged; disciplinary action against unnamed employees; SAP controls review.

bullets: **FY25:** EBITDA fell ₹213 cr, of which ~₹170 cr was the inventory correction (₹220.5 cr at Mar-25 less ₹50.2 cr already at Mar-24). Reported profit still rose to ₹415 cr because of a ₹193 cr deferred-tax credit (ACIL merger) and the ₹83 cr gain on the travel unit: ₹277 cr of one-offs, ~2.5x the underlying ~₹110 cr.

**FY26:** no inventory charge, but standalone exports fell 20% (US tariffs, Class 8 down 13-14%), energy and freight costs rose, depreciation (+23%) and interest (+27%) jumped as the new press lines and casting plant were commissioned, and the wheel JV lost ₹18 cr before production. Exceptional items netted −₹11 cr (labour codes −₹9 cr; an electricity-duty refund of +₹42 cr offset by a ₹42 cr provision on export receivables).

**Forensic work:** the fact-finding study was done by independent external agencies and included forensic imaging of devices and interviews of SAP custodians; it found erroneous entries and unrecorded rejections, not misappropriation. The joint auditors (S.R. Batliboi, S.K. Naredi) signed FY25 and FY26 accounts with the effects booked; there is no open restatement as of 30-Sep-2026.

**For valuation (PLAYBOOK §4):** FY25 and FY26 are trough years on EPS before one-offs (₹6.07 and ₹3.9, both below half of FY24's ₹16.1), so the house rule leaves the forward P/E for those years out of our median. On reported EPS only FY26 is a trough: FY25's one-offs would let a year of inflated earnings into the history.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** the collapse was mostly operational (inventory errors, exports, a capex bulge) dressed up and then exposed by one-offs. Nothing found so far points to fraud, and Q1FY27 shows the operating recovery. But a company that overstated stock by ~5% of revenue for a year without noticing has to earn back the market's trust in its numbers: we flag accounting RED until a clean FY27.

sections.title: Earnings quality: a restatement, one-off tax credits and a convenient provision

bullets: **Inventory overstatement (FY24-25).** ₹220.5 cr at Mar-25 (~5.5% of FY25 revenue), ₹50.2 cr at Mar-24; FY24 restated. Found by the physical count, quantified by independent agencies, booked in FY25. Controls (SAP access, manual entries) were tightened in FY26.

**One-off tax and gains.** FY25 profit included a ₹187 cr deferred-tax asset on ACIL's losses and an ₹83 cr discontinued-operations profit (travel unit sold for ₹128 cr). FY26 book tax was 14.5% of PBT. We tax forecasts at 25.5-26%; cash tax will stay lower while ACIL's losses are used, which helps cash flow, not EPS.

**A matched provision in Q4FY26.** A ₹42 cr refund of excess electricity duty was booked as exceptional income and a ₹42 cr expected-credit-loss provision on export receivables as an exceptional charge in the same quarter. The CFO said the company "did not want to carry it into our profit", that the amount is "totally receivable", and that it "will help us in future": a write-back later would flatter a future quarter.
**Cash conversion swings.** Operating cash flow was ₹33 cr in FY25 (working capital absorbed ₹362 cr) and ₹840 cr in FY26 (₹237 cr released). Inventory still runs at ~210 days on Screener's measure.
**JV accounting.** The 51% wheel JV is equity-accounted (joint control): its revenue, capex and debt stay off RKFL's balance sheet; only the profit share shows (−₹18 cr in FY26).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: RED.** The overstatement was errors, not fraud, and it has been booked; but it lasted a full year, ratings were cut or put on negative outlook, FY24 had to be restated, and the Q4FY26 provision shows management managing the profit line. We would move to AMBER after a clean FY27 audit with stable inventory days.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a recovery worth watching, not paying 28.8x Sep-28E for; SELL

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's second-largest forger, two-thirds domestic and mostly trucks, coming out of a bad two years (an inventory overstatement, US tariffs, a capex bulge) with new press, casting and wheel capacity to fill, ~₹1,900 cr of net debt and a family that put ₹405 cr of fresh equity in.

**What you are paying:** 33.1x our FY28E and 28.8x Sep-28E EPS. On normal earnings the stock traded at 7-17x forward in 2021-23; the own median since 2021 on EPS before one-offs is 14.6x, and auto-component stocks were below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. That gives 13.5x and {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): SELL. Kinder readings of the history (20x on reported EPS, 24.5x adding back the inventory charge) still give ₹490-600.

**This is mostly a valuation call.** The street (D&B ₹663, consensus average ₹634; average ₹649) is near the price; our EPS is a little lower and our multiple, derived from the stock's own history, is half of what the market pays.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Ramkrishna Forgings, consolidated, Rs crore, Screener basis. Revenue growth comes from the three-line build below (standalone domestic, standalone exports, subsidiaries and other net of eliminations), synced by RKFORGE.ctx.js. EBITDA margin is on the company basis (before the share of the rail-wheel JV, which we carry in other income). Shares: 18.557 cr after the 24-Sep-2026 warrant conversion (RKFORGE.patch.js); the Rs202.7 cr of warrant money received after Mar-26 is in the Mar-26 opening balance sheet.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the build. FY27E ~+20%: Q1FY27 +19.8% (standalone domestic +20%, exports +11%, subsidiaries +49%); Q2FY26 was the tariff-hit base (exports -32% YoY), so Q2-Q3 growth is easy; management expects 'almost 20% plus' export growth, Rs400-500 cr more casting revenue, Mexico from Q3 and higher press/casting utilisation. FY28E-29E: utilisation rising from 68% (Q1FY27) towards 80%, which management says is the point of the next capex. Management's Rs8,000 cr FY29 target (22-25% CAGR) is ~20% above our FY29E: the same target was set for FY28 and slipped a year.
assumptions._marginWhy: Company basis (before the JV share). FY26 15.2% (14.8% on Screener's basis, which nets the JV loss), Q4FY26 17.1%, Q1FY27 18.0% with a 54% gross margin. Management promises improvement 'every quarter' and wants the old 21-22% back but gives no range; energy, gas and shipping costs (West Asia conflict) are not passed on and the new casting, Mexico and press capacity run below normal use. We stop ~2.5pp short of the FY22-24 margins: 18.3% / 19.0% / 19.3%.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27: ~Rs350 cr guided (Q1FY27 call; Q4 call Rs300-400 cr incl. ~Rs50 cr into the wheel JV). FY28: no major capex until end-FY28 by management's account, but Rs10-20 cr for Inconel/titanium heating and maintenance on a Rs4,000 cr gross block: Rs350 cr. FY29: the next growth phase that management says it will announce at end-FY28: Rs450 cr. FY24-26 actual (cash flow, investing): Rs1,117 / 912 / 929 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 Rs333 cr; Q1FY27 Rs99 cr (Rs396 cr annualised) after the Q4FY26 capitalisation of the new press lines and the casting plant. The engine depreciates capex at once and holds CWIP flat; the rate gives ~Rs410 cr in FY27E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt (~Rs1,900 cr at Jun-26 per the CFO), so no treasury yield; deposit interest sits in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged. (1) Recurring other income ~Rs12 cr a year: FY26 Rs13.1 cr before exceptional items (AR FY26), Q1FY27 Rs3 cr; FY28-29E Rs12 / 14 cr. (2) Share of the 51% rail-wheel JV (equity method): FY26 -Rs17.9 cr before commercial production; FY27E -Rs8 cr (samples in Aug-26, bulk supply from Sep/Oct-26 against a 40,000-wheel FY27 offtake), FY28E +Rs8 cr, FY29E +Rs16 cr as 80,000+ wheels a year run through a 2.3 lakh-wheel plant. Totals Rs4 / 20 / 30 cr. Screener's TTM other income (Rs2 cr) is after exceptional items (FY26 -Rs10.7 cr net).
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest (term loans, working capital, bill discounting, leases)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs212 cr; Q1FY27 Rs57 cr. Net debt Rs1,990 cr (Mar-26) to Rs1,900 cr (Jun-26); management targets ~Rs1,500 cr by Mar-27, helped by Rs202.7 cr of promoter warrant money (Jun and Sep-2026). ~Rs57 / 55 / 52 / 50 cr a quarter in FY27, then Rs180 / 165 cr as net debt falls towards ~1x EBITDA.
assumptions._taxWhy: Statutory 25.17% (new regime). FY26 book tax 14.5% (deferred-tax adjustments) and FY25 a Rs193 cr credit (deferred tax asset on ACIL's losses): both one-offs. Q1FY27 27.6%. Book tax 26% / 25.5% / 25.5%; cash tax stays lower while the ACIL losses are used.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 Rs1/share (25% of a depressed profit); FY23-25 payout 9-14% (Screener). Deleveraging comes first: 12%.

build._note: Revenue build (Rs crore). Base FY26 from the Q4FY26/Q1FY27 investor presentations: standalone domestic Rs2,541.5 cr, standalone exports Rs1,186.6 cr; other = consolidated revenue (Rs4,238.1 cr) less the two (export incentives, subsidiaries net of eliminations). Checked against model revenue in RKFORGE.ctx.js.
build._why: Domestic: Q1FY27 +20%; quarterly path ~Rs735 / 690 / 760 / 840 cr against Rs611 / 516 / 662 / 752 cr a year earlier; CV demand firm (FY26 CV retail +11.7%; ICRA sees +4-6% in FY27), new casting line inside RKFL, PV/2W orders (Rs278 cr in Q1) and trailer axles (~Rs120 cr to ~Rs250 cr). Then +15% / +12% as press use rises towards 85%. Exports: FY26 -20% (US tariffs, Class 8 down 13-14%); Q1FY27 +11%; base quarters Rs278 / 271 / 319 cr; management 'almost 20% plus': we take +18%, then +15% / +13% on the order book (Rs2,800 cr of programme revenue for FY28 in the Q4 deck). Other (subsidiaries net): Q1 +49%; castings (RCSL), Mexico from Q3: +30% / +20% / +15%.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity. With net debt ~Rs1,700 cr against a ~Rs13,000 cr market value (D/V ~12%), a cost of equity of ~13.4% (beta 1.15, cyclical CV forgings) and post-tax debt cost ~6.8% give a WACC of ~12.6%; beta 1.0 sets the discount rate at 12.5%, close to that WACC.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: middle of the house range; forgings grow with CVs, industrial capex and railways, with no pricing power above inflation.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~13% to 7% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 18% steady-state EBITDA margin: FY22-24 averaged ~21.6%, FY25-26 13.9-15.2%; we sit between.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 6% of revenue in steady state (FY22-26: 15-30%, a build-out phase); depreciation 5.5%.
